info.name: Dokiments
info.description: Local API testing collection for the Firestore-backed routes built in Phase 0/1 (see docs/api-templates-documents.md). Auth is a session cookie, not a bearer token — Postman's built-in cookie jar handles it automatically once you run "Sign in", so no manual header wiring is needed between requests in this collection.

request.description: Establishes the session cookie (dokiments-session) that every other request in this collection relies on. Response body is { user: AuthUser } only — tokens never leave the server. Check the collection's Cookies panel for localhost after sending this to confirm the cookie was set. If DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true is set in .env.local, any email/password works and you'll get a fake session with role: "special" — useful for testing everything except the seed script, which needs a real superadmin account. promoCode is optional: when present it is redeemed after the credentials are accepted, and the outcome comes back as promo: "applied" | "already_redeemed" | "invalid" | "failed" next to the user. It never affects whether the sign-in itself succeeds — send a wrong code with a correct password to confirm you still get 200, with promo: "invalid". Omit the field and no promo key is returned at all.

First leg of Google sign-in — generates a CSRF state, seals it with the sanitised `next` path into a short-lived dokiments-oauth-state cookie, then 302s to Google's OAuth consent screen. Open this URL in an actual browser tab, not "Send" in Postman — completing it requires a real interactive Google login, and Postman can't drive that consent screen. Returns a redirect to /sign-in?error=google_failed instead if GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET aren't set in .env.local. promoCode is optional and sealed into that same state cookie, so a code typed on the form isn't lost by choosing Google — Google never sees it. The callback redeems it once the account exists and appends ?promo=<outcome> to the redirect, which PromoStatusBanner renders on arrival. It is capped at 64 characters before sealing so an oversized value can't produce a cookie the browser refuses.

item.name: Google callback (browser only, not directly callable)

request.description: Second leg of Google sign-in — Google redirects here itself with real `code`/`state` query params after consent; this entry exists for reference only and can't be usefully sent from Postman (it needs the dokiments-oauth-state cookie set by "Continue with Google" in the same browser, plus a `code` that's only valid once and only from that same flow). On success it exchanges `code` for a Google id_token, signs into Firebase via accounts:signInWithIdp, writes the dokiments-session cookie exactly like "Sign in" does, and 302s to the `next` path. Same 400/401-style failures all collapse to a redirect to /sign-in?error=google_failed — check the server terminal for the real cause (state mismatch, Google token exchange failure, or Firebase rejecting the id_token, most commonly because GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET don't match the Web client Firebase has on file for the Google provider).

Returns { user: AuthUser } if the session cookie is valid, or 401 null otherwise. Useful to confirm you're actually signed in before testing a protected route, and to check which role/tier the current session has.

Destroys the session cookie. Run this between test scenarios to reset to a signed-out state, then use "Unauthorised (401) check" under each resource folder to confirm routes reject the request correctly.

Updates the display name (Firebase Auth) and extended profile fields (Firestore). Returns { user: AuthUser } with the full updated profile — the client writes this straight into the session query cache instead of refetching GET /api/auth/me.

Changes the account password via Firebase and rotates the session's idToken/refreshToken. If the session is too old for this sensitive operation, Firebase rejects it and this route returns 403 { code: "REAUTH_REQUIRED", error } — the client responds by prompting for the current password (see "Reauthenticate") and retrying this same request.

Verifies the current password against the signed-in user's own email (taken from the session, never from the request body) and rewrites the session cookie with fresh tokens. Recovers from a 403 REAUTH_REQUIRED response on a sensitive action like "Update password" — call this first, then retry the original request.
Public, unauthenticated route — sends a Firebase password-reset email. Always returns { ok: true } regardless of whether the address is registered, to avoid leaking which emails have accounts.

GET /api/templates — full active catalog plus the active style list. Session required (401 without one). Response shape: { templates: MarketplaceTemplate[], styles: TemplateStyle[] }, both sorted by the seeded sortOrder field. See docs/api-templates-documents.md.

item.name: List catalog filtered by style + tier

request.description: Same route with optional query filters — these only filter `templates`, not `styles` (styles is always the full active list). Try an invalid value (e.g. styleId=nonsense) to confirm the Zod query validation returns 400, not a silent empty result.
GET /api/templates/:id. Try a nonexistent ID (e.g. does-not-exist) to confirm you get 404 { error: "Template not found." }, not a 500.

Run this AFTER "Sign out" (or in a fresh incognito-style environment with no prior sign-in) to confirm the route actually rejects an unauthenticated Postman request with 401 { error: "Unauthorised." } — this is the concrete scenario withSession was built to close.
GET /api/saved-templates — the signed-in user's saved-template list (empty array for a brand-new user). Session required.

POST /api/saved-templates — saves one template, as a single-document upsert on users/{uid}/savedTemplates/{templateId}. Returns 201 on a new save, 200 if already saved (both idempotent, not errors). Run "List saved templates" afterwards to confirm the write landed. Try a template above your account's tier (e.g. a gold-tier template while signed in as a free user) to confirm you get 403 { error: "Your plan does not include this template." } — this is the server-side tier re-validation check, which a client-side-only check would not catch from a direct Postman request.
DELETE /api/saved-templates/:templateId. Returns 204 with an empty body whether or not the template was actually saved (idempotent delete). Run "List saved templates" afterwards to confirm it's gone.
Run AFTER "Sign out" to confirm this route also 401s without a session, same as the templates catalog check.
GET /api/documents — the signed-in user's documents (empty array for a brand-new user). Session required.
Same route with the optional templateId filter.

POST /api/documents — creates a document, snapshotting the template's current name/style/fields onto it (templateSnapshot). Copy the returned document.id into the documentId collection variable to use the requests below. Try a nonexistent templateId to confirm you get 404 { error: "Template not found." }. Try more than 50 keys in `values`, or a value longer than 20,000 characters, to confirm the size-bound validation returns 400 rather than writing an oversized document.
GET /api/documents/:id. Requires documentId to be set (from "Create a document"'s response). Try a nonexistent ID to confirm 404 { error: "Document not found." }.

PATCH /api/documents/:id — partial update, name and/or values. Try sending {} (neither field) to confirm 400 { error: "Invalid request body." }. Run "Get one document" afterwards to confirm templateId/templateSnapshot are unchanged — this route must never touch them.
DELETE /api/documents/:id. Returns 204 with an empty body whether or not the document existed (idempotent delete).
Run AFTER "Sign out" to confirm this route also 401s without a session.

GET /api/clients — the signed-in user's client book, newest first (empty array for a brand-new user). Session required. Unlike saved templates there is no tier gate and no count limit on this collection: clients are private reference data, not an entitlement.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Maya Chen",
  "companyName": "Northline Studio",
  "email": "maya@northline.com",
  "phone": "+230 5 123 4567",
  "address": "12 Rue La Bourdonnais, Port Louis",
  "brn": "C12345678",
  "nationalId": ""
}

request.description: POST /api/clients — creates one client with a server-generated ID (client_…). Returns 201 { client }. Copy the returned id into the clientId collection variable to run the PATCH/DELETE requests below. name, companyName, email and phone are required; address, brn and nationalId are optional and default to "". Try omitting "name", or sending "email": "nope", to confirm you get 400 { error: "Invalid request body." } — the validation details are logged server-side only and never returned to the caller.

PATCH /api/clients/:clientId — partial update; only the fields you send change, and updatedAt is bumped. Send {} to confirm you get 400 (at least one field is required). Point clientId at a value that was never created to confirm you get 404 rather than a newly-created partial record — Firestore's REST PATCH is an upsert, so the route reads the document before writing specifically to prevent that.

DELETE /api/clients/:clientId. Returns 204 with an empty body whether or not the client existed (idempotent delete). Documents already prepared for this client are unaffected — their recipient details were copied into the document's own values at fill time, not referenced.
Run AFTER "Sign out" to confirm this route also 401s without a session.

GET /api/promo-redemptions — the promo codes this account has redeemed; this is what the Launch Promo card in Settings reads. Returns { redemptions: [] } for an account that has redeemed nothing, which includes every account created before this feature shipped — absence of a record IS "not redeemed", so no back-fill was needed. Each entry is { code, promoId, redeemedAt }, where promoId is the campaign slug (launch-2026) and is also the Firestore document ID.

POST /api/promo-redemptions — redeems the launch code for this account. Expect 201 { redemption } the first time. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace, so setting promoCode to "  vishdok2026! " is accepted and the canonical "ViSHDOK2026!" is what gets stored — worth trying, then confirming with "List redemptions". The write is a create-only Firestore PATCH (currentDocument.exists=false) against users/{uid}/promoRedemptions/launch-2026, and firestore.rules grants create but neither update nor delete there, so once-per-account is a database guarantee rather than something this route enforces on its own.

Send immediately after "Redeem the promo code" succeeded. Expect 409 { error: "This promo code has already been used for your account." } — the once-per-account rule. Note it is per account, not global: sign in as a different user and the same code redeems fine.

Expect 400 { error: "Invalid promo code." }. The code is matched server-side against the registry in src/lib/promo/promo-codes.ts — the browser knows the code (it's printed on the sign-in page by design, so it isn't a secret) but never decides the outcome. A whitespace-only value gives this same 400 rather than a generic "Invalid request body.", which is why the Zod schema deliberately doesn't trim.
Run AFTER "Sign out" to confirm this route also 401s without a session.
